name: A Madrid courtyard

place_source.title: Wikidata: Madrid (Q2807), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A traditional Madrid patio courtyard: stone paving, potted orange and olive trees, climbing jasmine and bougainvillea on whitewashed walls, a central fountain, visited by sparrows, magpies, parakeets and swifts by day, geckos and hedgehogs by night.

facts.text: Madrid has a hot-summer Mediterranean climate (Köppen Csa) with dry summers and mild winters.

source.title: Wikipedia: Madrid
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Madrid", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Madrid sits at 663 m above sea level, making it one of the highest capitals in Europe.

source.title: Wikidata: Madrid (Q2807), elevation above sea level

facts.text: The city's public centroid is at 40.42°N, 3.70°W in the Centro district.
Monk parakeets (Myiopsitta monachus) established feral populations in Madrid in the 1980s and now number thousands across the city's parks and gardens.

source.title: Wikipedia: Monk parakeet
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Monk parakeet", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Spotless starlings (Sturnus unicolor) are endemic to the Iberian Peninsula and replace the common starling across Spain, including urban Madrid.

source.title: Wikipedia: Spotless starling
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Spotless starling", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Common swifts (Apus apus) scream over Madrid's rooftops from May to August, nesting in cavities under eaves and roof tiles of historic buildings.

source.title: Wikipedia: Common swift
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Common swift", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Moorish geckos (Tarentola mauritanica) are common on Madrid's walls and ruins, hunting insects around streetlights at night.

source.title: Wikipedia: Moorish gecko
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Moorish gecko", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Iberian green frogs (Pelophylax perezi) breed in Madrid's park ponds, fountains and irrigation channels from March to June.

source.title: Wikipedia: Iberian green frog
